h1: Custom Garage Builders in Calgary: Oversized, Tall and Heated Garages
heroSub: Independent Calgary builders quote oversized-door, tall-wall, triple-bay and heated garages. Get two or three written quotes that price the same specification, then compare them line by line.
introHtml:
Custom garage builders in Calgary are independent firms, and this site puts you in touch with them. It builds nothing, pulls no permits and holds no licence; the builder who quotes your job contracts directly with you. This page lays out what a custom garage involves, so the quotes you collect describe the same building.

Custom usually means one or more of these: a door bigger than standard for a truck or RV, walls tall enough for a hoist or lift, a third bay, a workshop with its own power, or insulation and heat so the space works in January. Each one changes the structure, the permit path or the electrical service, and each shows up as a separate line on a quote. The sections below name those lines, with the prices Calgary builders publish and the City rules that set the limits. Every figure is attributed to whoever published it, and none of them is a quote from this site.

features.title: Oversized and tall doors
features.desc: One Calgary builder lists 18 x 7 ft and 18 x 8 ft insulated steel doors and a 9 ft ceiling as add-ons to its packages. Write down the clear opening you need instead of asking for 'oversized'.

features.title: Wall height for a lift or hoist
features.desc: The Land Use Bylaw sets 4.6 m overall and 3.0 m at the eaveline for a garage. Taller than that is a development permit application, and the City gives no guarantee of approval.

features.title: Triple bays and long layouts
features.desc: Builders advertise triples at sizes such as 30 x 24 ft and 36 x 20 ft. Over 55 m² (592 sq ft) the City wants an engineer-designed slab unless the foundation goes 1.2 m below grade.

features.title: Workshop power
features.desc: Advertised packages run from a 15 amp service to a 240V 30A or 40-amp subpanel. A new garage always needs a separate electrical permit, and only a Master Electrician can pull it for a contractor.

features.title: Insulation and heat
features.desc: Calgary builders price insulation, drywall, a gas unit heater or in-floor heat as separate add-ons. A gas heater also needs a gas permit.

features.title: Storage attics and lofts
features.desc: Calgary's bylaw allows an attic inside the single storey, reached by a removable ladder, with no windows and a 1.5 m maximum height. Rocky View County treats a second floor or mezzanine as a site-specific engineering job.

sections.heading: Where the City draws the line on size and height
sections.html:
Calgary's Land Use Bylaw 1P2007 limits an accessory residential building, which includes a detached garage, to one storey, 4.6 m from the finished floor and 3.0 m at any eaveline. The City's garage page adds that a development permit is required if the garage is higher than 4.6 m (15 ft 1 in), if the height from the parking surface to where the wall meets the roof truss is over 3 m (9 ft 10 in), if it is larger than 75 m² (807 sq ft), or if it is larger than the house. A development permit comes with no guarantee of approval.

The City's stated timelines are approximately 7 days for a building permit, and 10 to 12 weeks when a development permit is also needed. Its 2026 fee for a new garage building permit is $333.84, and a development permit for a design that does not meet every Land Use Bylaw rule is $550. The City says timelines depend on volumes and on how complete the application is.

  • Slab size: a slab over 55 m² (592 sq ft) needs a professional engineer's design unless it sits on a concrete foundation 1.2 m below grade, per the City.
  • Trades: every new garage needs an electrical permit, and a new gas line for a heater needs a gas permit.
  • Trusses: Rocky View County says all truss profiles and layouts must be stamped by a licensed Alberta engineer, and Airdrie says truss specifications must carry an Alberta Registered Engineer's seal as of 1 March 2026.
  • Other municipalities: Airdrie caps garage height at 5 m (16 ft 5 in) or the height of the house, whichever is smaller, and Cochrane sets 4.6 m for a peaked roof. See Airdrie, Cochrane and Rocky View County.

These rules change, and the City's own pages say they have no legal status. Confirm every number with the City or Town before you design around it.

sections.heading: What drives the price of a custom garage up
sections.html:
Published package prices describe a standard wood-frame garage. Custom work starts where those packages stop, and the builders who publish figures point to the same drivers: span, door size, slab, electrical service, and insulation and heat. The figures below come from different firms and do not agree with each other, which is the reason to collect written quotes. For the standard-size baseline, see garage building cost in Calgary and garage packages.

  • Span and bays: Venkor Group advertises a 24 x 24 double from $34,988 and a 30 x 24 triple from $48,606, GST not stated. Corsac Construction advertises a 36 x 20 triple from $49,000 + GST and says stamped structural drawings are required for the pad.
  • Oversized and tall-door builds: Precision Construction & Decora gives a typical market range of $90,000 to $140,000+ for an oversized, triple or tall-door garage (26 ft+ wide or extra ceiling height). BVM Builders advertises $85,000 to $120,000 for an unheated 26 x 28 oversized double.
  • Doors: Prime Garage Doors Calgary lists insulated steel double doors at $2,099 to $3,399 installed and custom wood or full-view glass doubles from $4,200. Falcon Contracting says premium doors add $600 to $1,800 over standard.
  • Slab and footings: Patriarch Construction says most pads run $4,500 to $8,000. Precision Construction & Decora says a double-garage slab with the right footings is usually $9,000 to $18,000 of the total.
  • Electrical: Precision Construction & Decora says a 240V outlet, subpanel or extra lighting runs $2,000 to $6,000. Calgary Garage Builders Ltd lists a 60 amp upgrade at $2,000 + GST.

Every figure above is what that firm advertises, not a market average and not a price from this site.

sections.heading: What to write into the specification so quotes compare
sections.html:
A quote is only comparable to the next one if both name the same items. Send every builder the same list, ask for the answers in writing, and treat a blank as a question, not as included. The list below covers what to pin down before you sign.

  • Door opening: width, height, number of doors, insulation value and opener. One Calgary door company lists insulated steel at R-12 to R-16, and one builder's heated-garage spec sets R-10 as the minimum.
  • Wall and ceiling height: state the wall height from the parking surface and the finished ceiling height. Venkor's packages list 9.5 ft walls; Corsac lists 8 ft walls with a 9 ft ceiling as an add-on. The City measures height from the finished floor.
  • Footprint and slab: exact outside dimensions, slab thickness (Venkor lists 4 in with a 6 in curb wall, Hammerhead 4 in with 10 in thickening), and whether engineered footings or a stamped slab design are in the price.
  • Roof structure: who supplies stamped truss drawings. The City asks for beam calculations or manufacturer truss layouts when the trusses rest on the garage door.
  • Power: panel amperage, number of 240V circuits, EV provision, and who pulls the electrical permit.
  • Insulation and heat: wall and ceiling insulation, vapour barrier, drywall, heater type and BTU rating, and the gas line if there is one.
  • Permits and drawings: who applies, since the City says a hired contractor applies, and whether drawings and permit fees are in the price. Venkor says City permits and design drawings are included in its quote; Corsac says the electrical permit and inspection are.
  • Exclusions and dates: demolition of an old garage (see garage replacement), site access, and written start and finish dates.

Service Alberta's contract checklist for prepaid contracting includes the itemized prices, the total, the payment terms and the commencement and completion dates. If a builder asks for money before the work is done, check the business in Service Alberta's licence search, which notes that a licence is not an endorsement. Then compare the quotes against a standard detached garage so you can see exactly what the custom items add.

sections.heading: Insulation, heat, power and the storage attic
sections.html:
A garage you work in through winter needs insulation, heat and power sized for the use. Calgary builders price these separately, and the published figures vary a lot, so ask each builder to itemize them.

  • Precision Construction & Decora: insulating and drywalling a double adds roughly $6,000 to $15,000, a forced-air or radiant tube heater adds $2,500 to $6,000, and in-floor heat is an extra $6,000 to $12,000.
  • BVM Builders: heating adds $8,000 to $22,000 to a standard double. It lists a gas unit heater at $3,500 to $6,000 installed and in-floor hydronic heat at $12,000 to $22,000.
  • Corsac Construction: a gas heater package at $6,600, which it says includes the heater, underground line and trenching, permitting and dedicated electrical service.
  • Polskiy Building (Okotoks page, each + GST): insulation and vapour barrier $1,700, drywall and insulation $3,000, gas line with permits $3,000, a 50,000 BTU gas heater $2,000, and 240V subpanel upgrades of $900 (40A), $1,000 (50A) or $1,200 (60A).

A storage attic is a different question. Calgary's bylaw allows an attic within the one permitted storey if it is reached by a removable ladder, has no windows, is used for the occupants' personal items, and is no more than 1.5 m high from attic floor to the underside of any rafter. Rocky View County says a garage with a second floor or mezzanine needs a site-specific engineered foundation design, so ask the County before you price one there. Call (403) 555-0162 to be matched with independent builders who quote custom garages.

faq.q: How tall can a custom garage be in Calgary?
faq.a: The Land Use Bylaw caps an accessory residential building at 4.6 m from the finished floor, 3.0 m at any eaveline and one storey. The City's garage page says a development permit is needed if the garage is higher than 4.6 m (15 ft 1 in), or if the height from the parking surface to where the wall meets the roof truss is over 3 m (9 ft 10 in). Approval is not guaranteed, so confirm with the City before you design around a lift.

faq.q: Does an oversized or triple garage need a development permit?
faq.a: The City lists a development permit for a garage larger than 75 m² (807 sq ft) or larger than the house, and for height or location relaxations. A 30 x 24 ft triple is 720 sq ft, under the 807 sq ft line, but height, setbacks or the 1.0 m gap to the house can still trigger one. The City's fee is $333.84 for a new garage building permit and $550 for a development permit, with about 7 days for the first and 10 to 12 weeks when a development permit is needed. Confirm your case with the City.

faq.q: How much does heating and insulating add?
faq.a: Precision Construction & Decora says insulating and drywalling a double adds roughly $6,000 to $15,000, plus $2,500 to $6,000 for a heater. BVM Builders says heating adds $8,000 to $22,000 to a standard double, and Corsac Construction advertises a $6,600 gas heater package. These are each firm's advertised figures and they differ, so ask every builder to itemize insulation, drywall, heater and gas line.

faq.q: How much more does an oversized or tall-door garage cost?
faq.a: Precision Construction & Decora gives a typical market range of $90,000 to $140,000+ for an oversized, triple or tall-door garage, and BVM Builders advertises $85,000 to $120,000 for an unheated 26 x 28 oversized double, or $95,000 to $138,000 heated. By comparison, Venkor Group advertises a standard 30 x 24 triple from $48,606. GST is not stated on the first three figures, and none of these is a quote from this site.

faq.q: How long does a custom garage take, and when should I ask for quotes?
faq.a: Sahi Contracting says most builds take 3 to 5 weeks once permits are in hand, and Falcon Contracting says 4 to 8 weeks from excavation to inspection. Add the City's 10 to 12 weeks if a development permit is needed. Hammerhead Construction says winter pours need heat, which adds cost, and that summer is busier, so winter is the time to gather two or three written quotes. Call (403) 555-0162 to get started.
